# Blueprint

> Find the right way to automate your work. Send an email and a video of one recurring job. Blueprint checks real robots against it by their published specifications and a cited track record, shows you the one that most likely fits and how sure it is, proves it in a simulation of your site, and then lets you share the job with deployment companies it has approved.

Blueprint starts with video of recurring work and drafts the job description from it. The site's answer comes first, minutes after the video is read: the robot that most likely fits, a runner-up from another maker, what was ruled out and why, published uses of those robots on similar work, and how sure Blueprint is. Blueprint then reconstructs the site in simulation, checks the picked robot there and runs public control policies on the job, and shows which did best with a cited statement of how far that can be trusted, or “held” for the simulation when it can't simulate that kind of job yet; the answer stays on the job page either way. Video is required before the site assessment can continue; a description alone does not replace it. With one click the site can share an anonymised job card, with the answer and the proof, with deployment companies Blueprint has approved, and Blueprint works alongside a deployment company on the real site. Customers contract with the deployment company, which installs and supports the system. Deployment partners and robot technology providers have separate reviewed application paths. The beta remains free for sites and partners, with no Blueprint cut of physical pilot costs. Simulation is a bounded estimate and never certifies physical performance or safety. Customer-reported pilot outcomes remain separate from authoritative scientific Physical Outcome Joins.

Robot teams register interest through the existing application to give Blueprint access to a policy or an integration. Applications remain pending until manual approval for a real site task; applying or creating an account does not grant access. Approved teams see only job cards sites chose to share. Blueprint runs each evaluation; a team supplies access to its policy or robot, or an integration, free during the beta. Teams do not run their own evaluations of a site's job. Approval does not guarantee a run or a deployment. Paid self-service evaluations and top-ups are disabled during the beta. Beta program: https://tryblueprint.io/beta. Contact: hello@tryblueprint.io.

## Evidence boundary

Customer wording uses “job” for the work a site wants automated and “task” for the specific robot action and its technical conditions. API fields and identifiers retain their existing names.

A Task Evaluation Run returns a decision or abstention. Pipeline owns method qualification and routing; physical outcomes remain distinct from simulation and generated evidence.

## Agent interfaces and compatibility

Current public/request tools are `blueprint.siteWorld.search`, `blueprint.catalog.search`, `blueprint.ask`, `blueprint.request.locationDraft`, `blueprint.siteWorld.get`, and `blueprint.siteWorld.launchReadiness`.

The historical read and hosted-session compatibility tools are `blueprint.commerce.order.get`, `blueprint.commerce.liveOrder.get`, `blueprint.commerce.entitlement.get`, `blueprint.commerce.entitlementReadiness`, `blueprint.session.create`, `blueprint.session.reset`, `blueprint.session.step`, `blueprint.session.runBatch`, `blueprint.session.control`, `blueprint.session.renderExplorer`, and `blueprint.session.export`. Historical availability does not make these current standalone products.

Team tools are `blueprint.team.me`, `blueprint.team.checkpoint.register`, `blueprint.team.checkpoint.list`, `blueprint.team.plan`, `blueprint.team.runs.start`, `blueprint.team.runs.release`, `blueprint.team.policy.get`, and `blueprint.team.policy.set`. Team account and checkpoint tools use a revocable per-team agent key bound to a verified Blueprint account. Early-access library admission remains required (403 `early_access_required` otherwise). During the free beta, paid planning, dry-run purchase, run-start and top-up APIs return 403 `paid_evaluations_disabled`, including requests with `confirm: true`. Offer your system for a job through the workspace; Blueprint runs it. Execution requires operator approval of the exact team, policy, task, current rights, expiry, one attempt, and a separate Blueprint-funded compute limit. Historical balances and receipts remain available under their original access controls.

Truth labels are `capture_grounded`, `provider_derived`, `generated`, `request_gated`, `protected_robot_team`, `legacy_commerce_read_only`, and `decision_or_abstention`.
